issues.issue: The prudent-person standard applies while a Master Servicer Event of Termination is uncured 'but only until such time as a successor Master Servicer shall have been appointed,' even though under Section 7.02 the Trustee itself becomes that successor. When the heightened standard ends, and whether it ends when the Trustee takes over, is unclear.

The opening sentence preserves the Trustee's liability 'for its own negligent action, its own negligent failure to act or its own willful misconduct,' while clause (i) provides that its duties are 'determined solely by the express provisions of this Agreement' with no implied covenants read against it. The scope of the negligence liability that survives the proviso is the question.

Clause (iv) requires investigation only if requested by Holders of 'not less than 25% of the Voting Rights allocated to each Class of Certificates,' which can be read as 25% of every Class or 25% in the aggregate. The threshold for compelling the Trustee to investigate is ambiguous.

The indemnity from the Trust covers four categories of loss but is followed by 'provided, that any such loss, liability or expense constitutes an "unanticipated expense incurred by the REMIC"' under the Treasury regulation, without saying whether that proviso qualifies only clause (iv) or all four. Read broadly the proviso would defeat most of the indemnity it follows.

The Trustee must have 'a credit rating of at least investment grade' without specifying whose rating, of what obligations, or by which agency. Whether the Trustee has ceased to be eligible, and must therefore resign immediately, cannot be determined from the requirement as stated.

The resignation sentence has no operative verb for its final clause — 'and acceptance by a successor trustee acceptable to the NIMS Insurer and the Certificate Insurer and in accordance with Section 8.08 meeting the qualifications set forth in Section 8.06' — so it is unclear whether successor acceptance is a condition of the resignation taking effect. The mechanics of a Trustee resignation are left incomplete.

The first sentence requires co-trustees to be 'approved by the Trustee, the Certificate Insurer and the NIMS Insurer' and says the Master Servicer and Trustee 'acting jointly shall' appoint them, while the next sentence lets the Trustee appoint alone if the others do not join within fifteen days. Whether the approvals are conditions or merely invitations is left unresolved.

The Trust Administrator is not relieved 'from liability for its own negligent action,' yet clause (i) confines its duties 'solely' to the express provisions with no implied obligations. What negligence remains actionable once implied duties are excluded is left open.

Clause (x) entitles the Trust Administrator to be reimbursed for discretionary litigation costs 'out of the Collection Account,' but Section 3.10(a) enumerates the permitted withdrawals from that account and gives that right only to the Master Servicer and Servicers. The two provisions cannot both be applied as written.

The Trust's indemnity of the Trust Administrator is qualified by the proviso that the loss 'constitutes an "unanticipated expense incurred by the REMIC"' under Treasury Regulations Section 1.860G-1(b)(3)(ii), with no indication whether that condition attaches to all three enumerated categories or only the last. The reach of the indemnity turns on that placement.

Eligibility requires 'a credit rating of at least investment grade' without identifying the rated obligations or the rating agency, yet loss of eligibility compels immediate resignation. The triggering condition has no ascertainable measure.
